title: Shortest Coupling-Robust Sets for Ordinal Individual Treatment Effects and the Price of Intervals
banked_reason: The contribution is graded subfield rather than field: paper_score_ceiling 6.9 < 7.4, with no bounded salvage in the current scope.
gap_reasons: The advertised remdesivir relevance remains prospective: the package reports no trial marginals, selected effect set, confidence-certified set, or coverage-level sensitivity analysis.
The min-cut handles evaluation of a fixed candidate, while the global optimization remains exponential enumeration, so scalability beyond small ordinal supports is not established.

Selection consistency is confined to a fixed-margin class that excludes positive-width neighborhoods of feasibility surfaces, and the inference result certifies validity without addressing efficiency.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the optimizer-wide Hall/rectangle normal form, complete ternary frontier, both sharp interval-price regimes and equality cases, exact finite computation, and the certification/selection results; the cited finite Strassen deficiency was verified from Koperberg's Proposition 6. The field claim collapsed on materiality rather than correctness: no delivered remdesivir analysis, exponential outer enumeration, and a separated-class selector theorem kept the package at subfield tier. A re-raise should add a real-data or scalable computational contribution rather than rerun the same mathematics.
tldr: Randomization identifies the two ordinal potential-outcome marginals but not their coupling. The note characterizes every shortest coupling-robust individual-effect set as a high-mass difference set, gives an exact boundary-safe ternary disconnectedness frontier, and proves a sharp missed elbow in the price of interval reporting: the worst multiplicative price is \((2L-1)/3\) when target coverage exceeds one half and \(L/2\) when target coverage is at most one half. The interval benchmark is the shortest completion of the anchor's marginal-robust validity criterion; comparison is direct on the anchor's stated coverage-level domain and extends the same functional through its omitted neighborhood and the elbow. Exact min-cut computation and simultaneous multinomial confidence-polytopes provide finite-sample certification and uniform selector recovery away from explicit tie surfaces.
gap: The closest ITE papers give sharp distributional bounds and optimize interval-valued reports, but no located result solves the outer cardinality optimization over arbitrary ordinal effect sets; Hall theory certifies a fixed support but does not solve that selection problem.
fill: The difference-set normal form, complete ternary frontier, sharp general-support interval price, and confidence-polytope inversion jointly deliver identification, geometry, computation, and honest reporting.
